title: Krakatau eruption, 1883

place.label: Krakatau volcano, Indonesia
place.basis: NCEI published volcano point for event 2429; one point stands for a whole volcano
place.coords_source: NOAA NCEI Significant Volcanic Eruptions Database, event 2429

date.label: Eruption date in the NCEI catalogue

facts.text: NCEI files this eruption as a caldera volcano and links it to a tsunami record.
Explosions on 27 August 1883 were heard about 5,000 km away; USGS calls it the loudest and farthest-travelled sound in recorded history.
The island, about 30 km² before the eruption, nearly vanished. About 25 km³ of material was thrown out and the eruption column rose above 30 km.
Dust carried into the stratosphere lowered global temperatures and caused vivid sunsets.
A new volcano, Anak Krakatau, appeared about 50 years later.
USGS says the 1991 Pinatubo eruption disturbed the atmosphere probably less than Krakatau 1883 and Tambora 1815 did.

claims.text: About 36,000 people died, most of them in the tsunami.

tiers.everyday: In August 1883 the Krakatau volcano in Indonesia blew apart. The explosions were heard about 5,000 km away, and the tsunami that followed killed tens of thousands of people.
tiers.student: NOAA NCEI lists the 27 August 1883 eruption of Krakatau at VEI 6, with 36,417 deaths in total. USGS gives about 36,000 and names the tsunami as the main cause. A USGS Volcano Watch article says about 25 km³ of material was thrown out, the island nearly vanished, and dust in the stratosphere lowered global temperatures.
